title: Eikev: love the stranger (Deuteronomy 10:19)
hookLine: "Love ye therefore the stranger; for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt"

cards: The first week somewhere new. A new school, a new job, a new country. Not knowing where the bathroom is, or which jokes are safe, or whether anyone will sit with you at lunch.
Everyone else moves easily through rules you can't see. A year later, that feeling is easy to lose. You become one of the ones who know where everything is.
The Torah, it seems, is worried about exactly that forgetting, because it comes back to this person, the stranger, again and again.

teach.h: GOD FEEDS AND CLOTHES THE STRANGER.
teach.b: Moses has just described God as great and mighty, the one who can't be bribed.

And then, of all the things to say next: "He doth execute justice for the fatherless and widow, and loveth the stranger, in giving him food and raiment." The God of everything is described by who God feeds and clothes.
And the next verse turns it into a command: "Love ye therefore the stranger; for ye were strangers in the land of Egypt." The Hebrew word is ger.
In the Torah, a ger is someone living among a people not their own: a resident foreigner, without land, without family nearby, easy to cheat.
Later, in rabbinic Hebrew, ger also came to mean a convert, someone who joins the Jewish people, and the rabbis read some of these verses about converts too.
Both meanings are about someone arriving from outside. The reason given isn't an argument. It's a memory.

teach.h: YE KNOW THE HEART OF A STRANGER.
teach.b: In Exodus it's said even more sharply: "for ye know the heart of a stranger." The people Moses speaks to didn't have to imagine it. Their families had lived it, in Egypt.
And the Torah keeps coming back to it.
The path met this count earlier in the year: the Talmud, in Bava Metzia, says the Torah warns about the stranger in thirty-six places, and some say forty-six.
One way to hear the repetition: the command isn't complicated. It's just easy to forget once you're the one who knows where everything is.

how: Jewish communities cite the command to love the stranger in teaching about welcoming converts and newcomers, and some Jewish organizations that work with refugees and immigrants cite these verses.

games.q: Moses has just called God great, mighty and unbribable. what does he say God does next?
o: loves the stranger, giving food and clothing.

practice: Go back to your own first week somewhere: the not knowing, the hoping someone would notice. Now look around your life as it is, a neighbor, a coworker, a family at school, someone just arrived in your country.
Picture one of them, and the one thing you know that they don't yet.

wordCard.voice: Eikev. Because, and heel. The portion that ends its teaching with the stranger, because you were strangers once.
